subject: E2E tail latency readiness — hosted vs incumbent (post-demo recap)
messages:
From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@ordinex.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-team@ordinex.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo + initial latency discussion

Thanks for the walkthrough today — helpful demo. A couple clarifying points from the engineering side before we lock next steps: 

- Our production traffic is mixed (chat + short completions). Typical payload sizes: 120–320 tokens incoming, responses average 180 tokens.
- Peak tail concerns: we see P99 end-to-end spikes when multiple long-context chats hit the same session key; suspect cache / KV pressure.
- Streaming is critical for our UX on streaming chat. We need smooth first-byte P95 < 300ms and steady tailing so the stream doesn't stall.

I attached our simplified traffic profile CSV (ordinex_traffic_profile_qps.csv) with QPS histogram and session-length buckets. Can you confirm whether Redwood hosted will: 
1) preserve per-session KV cache semantics across concurrent requests for the same conversation id, and
2) whether streaming requests will be routed to warm workers to avoid cold-start stalls?

Also, what's your recommended test harness / synthetic workload to validate end-to-end P95/P99 against our current provider? We want an apples-to-apples run.

Thanks,
Tim
Lead Platform Engineer, Ordinex

--

Subject: Re: Demo + initial latency discussion — follow-up and asks

Tim — great questions and thanks for the CSV. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap of needs you called out:
- P95 first-byte (streaming) target: < 300 ms
- P99 end-to-end tail: target TBD by you, current pain is spikes during concurrent long-context reuse
- Throughput envelope: baseline 400 QPS, burst to 2.5k QPS; concurrency on some routes can hit 120 concurrent streams
- Preservation of per-session KV/cache affinity and no cold-start stalls for streaming sessions

Immediate asks we can action: 
1) Engineering alignment call (30 min) to confirm exact session affinity semantics and mapping to our routing policies — Aditya and Priyom to join.
2) We’ll propose a concrete SLO matrix (p95/p99 buckets, warm vs cold, streaming vs non-streaming) and a test harness recipe. See attachment: slo_matrix_proposal_kp-6371.xlsx (draft).
3) A small hosted PoC: 1k QPS steady, 2.5k burst for 10 mins, streaming enabled; we will instrument token-level breakdowns and request traces.

Questions for you before we schedule the eng call: 
- Can you confirm the exact P99 target you need to sign off on a migration (e.g., <500ms end-to-end, or <800ms acceptable)?
- Is data residency (US-only) required?

We’ll wait for your confirmation and then Ben will own scheduling.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Demo + initial latency discussion — engineering notes and test plan

Tim — quick engineering note and proposed technical checklist for the PoC: 

Observations (from today + your CSV):
- The session-length distribution suggests heavy tail on conversation length; that maps to larger KV cache state and higher token generation time per request.
- If multiple concurrent requests target the same conversation id, our runtime can either serialize KV access or use lock-free snapshots depending on model footprint; we'll need to align on semantics.

Proposed PoC test plan (apples-to-apples):
- Workload synthesis: replay CSV-derived QPS histogram with two traffic shapes: (A) chat-heavy streaming (60% of traffic) and (B) short completion calls (40%). Use real token lengths per your CSV.
- Concurrency sweep: run tests at steady 400 QPS, then ramp to 1k, 1.8k, and 2.5k with 5 minute holds. For each stage, sample p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and end-to-end.
- Warm vs cold: include a warm-run (pre-warm pool for 10 mins) and a cold-run (scale-from-zero scenario) to capture differences in cold-start tail.
- Session-affinity check: create targeted scenario where 100 conversation ids each receive 3 concurrent requests and measure KV lock latency and p99 amplification.
- Instrumentation: token-level cost/time, worker CPU/GPU utilization, network egress time, and runtime queueing delay. Redwood will provide tracing links and a read-only dashboard for the test window.

Implementation notes: 
- Streaming: we will pin streaming connections to warm workers for the PoC so stalls are minimized; persistent-worker policy for the test only. In prod we can discuss hybrid policies.
- Batching: we’ll run both continuous-batching enabled and batching-disabled variants to show tradeoffs for p95 vs cost.

Action items assigned: 
- Aditya: build and share the k6/JMeter recipe that replays the CSV shapes and concurrency scenarios (ETA 48h).
- Priyom: set up the hosted test pool with persistent worker pinning and the tracing hooks (ETA 72h).
- Kimberly/Ben: align commercial guardrails (SLA floor, cost estimate) based on test results.

If that sounds good I’ll kick off the harness and send a calendar invite for the alignment call.

-Aditya
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
